passages.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments, according to Sheminith. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon:
This psalm is for the choirmaster.
The psalm uses stringed instruments.
The music follows the style called Sheminith.
David wrote this psalm.

passages.text: O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
The musicians played stringed instruments.
They played according to Sheminith.
David prayed to the LORD.
He said, “O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger.”
He said, “Do not discipline me in Your wrath.”
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ בִּ֭נְגִינוֹת עַֽל־ הַשְּׁמִינִ֗ית מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ יְֽהוָ֗ה אַל־ בְּאַפְּךָ֥ תוֹכִיחֵ֑נִי וְֽאַל־ בַּחֲמָתְךָ֥ תְיַסְּרֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to the LORD.
David asks the LORD to show him mercy.
David says he is weak.
David asks the LORD to heal him.
David says his bones hurt greatly.
passages.original: חָנֵּ֥נִי יְהוָה֮ כִּ֤י אֻמְלַ֫ל אָ֥נִי רְפָאֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֖י נִבְהֲל֣וּ עֲצָמָֽי׃

passages.text: My soul is deeply distressed. How long, O LORD, how long?
passages.sermon: David speaks to the LORD.\r\nDavid feels deep distress in his soul.\r\nDavid asks the LORD, "How long will this last?"
passages.original: וְ֭נַפְשִׁי נִבְהֲלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאַתְּ יְ֝הוָ֗ה עַד־ מָתָֽי׃

passages.text: Turn, O LORD, and deliver my soul; save me because of Your loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
The speaker cries out to the LORD.
The speaker asks the LORD to turn back to him.
The speaker asks the LORD to deliver his soul.
The speaker asks the LORD to save him.
The speaker gives a reason.
The speaker says the LORD has loving devotion.
The speaker asks the LORD to save him because of this loving devotion.
passages.original: שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה חַלְּצָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י ה֝וֹשִׁיעֵ֗נִי לְמַ֣עַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?
passages.sermon:
God, You are the subject of this statement.
No one remembers You in death.
No one praises You from Sheol.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
People cannot honor You there.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֵ֣ין בַּמָּ֣וֶת זִכְרֶ֑ךָ בִּ֝שְׁא֗וֹל מִ֣י יֽוֹדֶה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping and drench my couch with tears.
passages.sermon:
David is the speaker.
David feels deep sorrow.
David groans often.
David becomes tired from his groaning.
David weeps every night.
David floods his bed with tears.
David drenches his couch with weeping.
passages.original: יָגַ֤עְתִּי׀ בְּֽאַנְחָתִ֗י אַשְׂחֶ֣ה בְכָל־ לַ֭יְלָה מִטָּתִ֑י בְּ֝דִמְעָתִ֗י עַרְשִׂ֥י אַמְסֶֽה׃

passages.text: My eyes fail from grief; they grow dim because of all my foes.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David suffers greatly.
Grief weakens David’s eyes.
David’s eyes grow dim.
David’s enemies cause this sorrow.
passages.original: עָֽשְׁשָׁ֣ה מִכַּ֣עַס עֵינִ֑י עָֽ֝תְקָ֗ה בְּכָל־ צוֹרְרָֽי׃

passages.text: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to his enemies.
David calls his enemies "workers of iniquity."
David tells all workers of iniquity to leave him.
David says, "Depart from me."
David explains why they must leave.
The LORD has heard David's weeping.
passages.original: ס֣וּרוּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי כָּל־ פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֥ע יְ֝הוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל בִּכְיִֽי׃

passages.text: The LORD has heard my cry for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer.
passages.sermon: The LORD is God.\r\nThe LORD has heard my cry for mercy.\r\nThe LORD accepts my prayer.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֣ע יְ֭הוָה תְּחִנָּתִ֑י יְ֝הוָ֗ה תְּֽפִלָּתִ֥י יִקָּֽח׃

passages.text: All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed; they will turn back in sudden disgrace.
passages.sermon:
All my enemies will feel shame.
All my enemies will feel fear.
They will turn back.
They will feel sudden disgrace.
passages.original: יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ׀ וְיִבָּהֲל֣וּ מְ֭אֹד כָּל־ אֹיְבָ֑י יָ֝שֻׁ֗בוּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ רָֽגַע׃
